exposure: Baseline fetal heart rate between 110 and 149 bpm
Baseline fetal heart rate between 150 and 160 bpm
baseline fetal heart rate between 150 and 160 bpm at 40 gestational weeks or beyond
cohort: 1004 singleton pregnancies with spontaneous onset of labor at 40 weeks gestation or beyond
finding: In fetuses at 40 weeks or beyond, an intrapartum fetal heart rate baseline between 150 and 160 bpm is associated with a higher incidence of labor complications, including meconium-stained amniotic fluid, cesarean section for fetal distress, neonatal acidemia, and adverse composite neonatal outcome.
mod_finding: Urgent/emergent cesarean section for suspected fetal distress was significantly higher in the group with a baseline fetal heart rate between 150 and 160 bpm.
